## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

content.text:
No — and this one is already a settled design decision, not an open call.

**What `.gitattributes` currently does here** — three `merge=ours` lines, one per GENERATED file, so a conflicting merge auto-resolves and the generator re-runs instead of a hand-merge. That's the only job it has in this repo.

**Why blanket-omitting `.claudinite/` would be wrong, in both senses of "omit":**

*As `linguist-vendored` / `linguist-generated`* (which is what actually drops files from checks — `vendoredSet` in `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs:90`): the vendored half is **already** out of scope, and deliberately not via attributes. `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs:428` filters `.claudinite/shared/` out of the file set structurally, and `vendoring/DESIGN.md:95` states the reason outright — "Deliberately a structural rule in the engine, **not** a `.gitattributes` / `linguist-vendored` convention: the exclusion must hold on any git host and any checkout." An attribute is a per-checkout convention; the engine rule holds even where `.gitattributes` was never delivered.

The other half is worse: `.claudinite/local/` is the repo's **own** authored code — 34 tracked files here, real `.mjs` checks with their tests, skills, `RULES.md`. Marking it vendored silently disables every check over it. And in *this* repo there is no `shared/` at all, so a blanket `.claudinite/**` line buys nothing and turns off checking of the entire local-pack tree.

*As `merge=ours`*: actively destructive. `.claudinite/local/packs/*/RULES.md` is append-only and written several times a day by the growth tasks — taking "ours" on a conflict drops the other side's appended lessons with nothing going red.

The one entry under `.claudinite/` that *should* exist is the narrow one that already does: `claudinite-rules.GENERATED.md merge=ours`, which `ensureRulesIndexMergeAttribute` (`engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs:242`) maintains automatically. That's the right granularity — per generated file, by the mechanism that owns the file.

> ✅ Answer: no. The vendored mount is already excluded structurally (by design, on purpose not via attributes), and `.claudinite/local/` is first-class repo code that must stay in scope. No change recommended.

Different answer for that half — and one genuinely open gap.

**For check scope: no entry, and deliberately so.** `.claudinite/shared/` is already dropped from every check's file set structurally, in `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs:428`, and `vendoring/DESIGN.md:95` says why in as many words: "Deliberately a structural rule in the engine, **not** a `.gitattributes` / `linguist-vendored` convention: the exclusion must hold on any git host and any checkout." An attribute is per-checkout convention; the engine rule holds in a bare clone, a non-GitHub host, a member whose `.gitattributes` was hand-edited. Adding one *for that purpose* would be the same fact stated in two places with nothing guarding the drift.

**For `merge=ours`: no.** A conflict on the mount isn't resolved by preferring either side — `vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs:12` is explicit that convergence is "unconditional and whole-set: shared/ is rebuilt from the set (stale files vanish, local edits revert)". `merge=ours` would pin a member on a half-old tree that reads as converged, and the anti-rewind guards fire before the write, not on a merge. The correct resolution is re-running the converge, which already happens.

**For Linguist and diff presentation: this is the real gap, and I think it's worth closing.** The vendor set is 642 files / ~6 MB of `.mjs` and Markdown landing in every member's `.claudinite/shared/`. In a member whose own code is Python, Swift, TypeScript — anything but JS — that mass can outweigh the project's own source by byte count and make GitHub label the repo JavaScript; and every PR that touches the mount renders the whole tree expanded instead of collapsed. `linguist-vendored` fixes both, and the canon already prescribes exactly this treatment for large committed non-project content, in `packs/git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md:155`. Nothing anywhere in the tree currently sets it for the mount.

Two things make it cheap: it has **no** interaction with the checks engine (the mount is filtered out of `scanned` before `vendoredSet` or `allFiles` ever see it, so the annotation changes no check's behavior), and there's already a carrier — `ensureRulesIndexMergeAttribute` in `engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs:242` maintains a `.gitattributes` line fleet-wide today, so a sibling `ensure` reaches every member without per-repo manual work.

So: the mount wants exactly one line, `\.claudinite/shared/** linguist-vendored`, for presentation only — never for scope, never `merge=ours`.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

input.title: Declare the shared mount linguist-vendored in every member's .gitattributes
input.body:
A member's `.claudinite/shared/` holds ~640 canon-owned files (several MB of `.mjs` and Markdown) that the member never authored. Nothing tells the git host that.

Two consequences, neither of which the engine's own exclusion covers:

- **Linguist mislabels the repo.** The mount outweighs a small member's own source by byte count, so a Python or Go member can read as a JavaScript repo.
- **Converge diffs render expanded.** A whole-set refresh shows every vendored file as reviewable content.

The check-scope exclusion is separate and stays where it is: `buildContext` (`engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs:428`) filters the mount prefix structurally, deliberately not attribute-driven (`vendoring/DESIGN.md`), so this line changes no check's behavior — the mount is already dropped before `git check-attr` is consulted. This is host-side presentation only.

The carrier exists: `ensureRulesIndexMergeAttribute` (`engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs:241`) already creates or appends `.gitattributes` in every member, at adoption and on every wiring converge. A sibling ensure lands beside it and reaches the fleet on the nightly converge.

The wiring converge now declares the mount `linguist-vendored`, beside the rules index's `merge=ours` line — reusing the `.gitattributes` edit bootstrap already performs, so the line reaches the fleet on the nightly converge with no new carrier.

Tests were written and watched failing first (`does not provide an export named 'MOUNT_VENDORED_ATTR'`), then made green. One of them asserts through real `git check-attr` against a real mount path, so a pattern that matched nothing could not pass as live. Full suite 2651/2651; world sweep 0 blocking.

Answering the narrower question, then what landed.

**`.claudinite/shared/` is the one part where an attribute does buy something** — but not the thing you might expect. Check scope is already handled structurally and deliberately so: `repo-context.mjs:428` filters the mount prefix out of the file set *before* `git check-attr` runs, because the exclusion has to hold on any host and any checkout. That's unchanged and unchallenged.

What the engine rule can't do is talk to the host. ~640 canon-owned files, ~6 MB of `.mjs` and Markdown, in every member — enough to make Linguist call a small Python or Go member a JavaScript repo, and enough to render a converge diff fully expanded. Only `.gitattributes` fixes either.

Your condition was met: bootstrap already edits `.gitattributes` — step 4's wiring converge calls `ensureRulesIndexMergeAttribute`, which creates or appends the file in every member at adoption and on every converge. So the new line rides an existing carrier rather than earning one.

```
Folders touched

engine/scheduler/  converge-wiring.mjs — new MOUNT_VENDORED_ATTR +
                   ensureMountVendoredAttribute, factored onto a shared
                   ensureAttributeLine with the existing merge=ours ensure;
                   added to the converge's change list.
engine-tests/      converge-wiring.test.mjs — idempotency test, plus one that
                   runs real `git check-attr` over a real mount path so a
                   pattern matching nothing can't pass as live.
vendoring/         DESIGN.md §6 — clause distinguishing the structural
                   check-scope rule from the host-side annotation.
```

Both tests were watched failing first (`does not provide an export named 'MOUNT_VENDORED_ATTR'`) before any implementation. Suite 2651/2651, world sweep 0 blocking (72 advisories, all pre-existing in `packs/tidy-repo/`).

Issue [#1261](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1261) → PR [#1263](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1263). I left `updates/pack-update.mjs` alone deliberately — that lane converges the rules index because a stale index mid-cycle degrades rule loading; the attribute has no equivalent urgency.

> ⚠️ Still open: PR [#1263](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1263) needs your review — merging it is a fleet-wide effect (every member's `.gitattributes` gains the line at its next converge).

name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
